- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d forecast).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then overshoot, followed by a sharp drop — suggesting overreaction to recent spikes.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; model fails to smoothly decay toward historical averages after peaks.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward higher values, especially when recent history is trending upward.
- Model reacts too aggressively to short-term volatility, leading to overcorrection or overshoot in mid-to-late forecast period.
- When true outcome declines sharply after a spike, model fails to adjust downward quickly — lagging correction.
- Forecasts often ignore the influence of recent low values (e.g., 3–5 days prior) in smoothing out downward trends.
- Model exhibits “memory decay” — fails to retain recent low prices as anchors for future forecasting.
- Overestimation is more pronounced when historical mean is rising — model assumes continuation rather than mean reversion.
- Forecasting should incorporate a decay factor for recent high values to prevent overconfidence in upward momentum.
